levels.title: Opioid LASA Pair Recognition
levels.description: Recognize look-alike and sound-alike counterparts among high-potency synthetic opioids.
levels.learningObjective: Identify documented ISMP confusable opioid counterparts.

questions.prompt: Which synthetic opioid is an ISMP-documented look-alike / sound-alike counterpart to fentanyl?
questions.explanation: fentanyl and ALfentanil share similar root letters but possess vastly different pharmacokinetic profiles.

questions.prompt: Which natural opiate is frequently confused with HYDROmorphone due to shared root names?
questions.explanation: HYDROmorphone is approximately 4-7 times more potent than morphine, making mix-ups extremely hazardous.

questions.prompt: Which opioid pairs with ALfentanil on the ISMP list of confused drug names?
questions.explanation: ALfentanil and SUFentanil are potent synthetic opioids that look and sound alike.

questions.prompt: Which synthetic opioid pairs with fentaNYL to form an ISMP look-alike pair differing in prefix and suffix capitalization?
questions.explanation: fentaNYL and SUFentanil differ by prefix SUF- vs suffix -NYL.

questions.prompt: Which opioid is a documented look-alike counterpart to HYDROmorphone?
questions.explanation: HYDROmorphone and oxyMORphone differ in their middle syllable and prefix.
